utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today, we are the 1st of October, 2008. I'd like to greet the representatives of the Prosecution, amongst others Ms. Dahl and Mr. Mundis, as well as associates. I would also like to greet Mr. Seselj and all the people assisting us. Mr. Seselj, I know that you have a number of housekeeping matters you would like to address. I personally would like to address one such matter; namely: It had been planned to sit tomorrow afternoon. We shall now hold our hearing at 8.30 tomorrow morning. At 12.00, the Judges need to attend an extraordinary plenary session which relates to a legal issue which might be of interest to you, i.e., the fact that a Trial Chamber may be authorised to appoint a counsel in the interests of justice, a counsel for the accused. This plenary session is extremely important, and I therefore wish to attend this meeting, as well as my colleagues, and we shall resume our hearing at 2.00 tomorrow and will run on until 4.00. Then we will have had a five-hour hearing, approximately. Today, we will stop at 20 past 6.00 because the Judges need to attend a meeting. There are a lot of meetings at the moment. Since their witness's testimony is high on the agenda, we need to start with this. I know you have three housekeeping matters you wish to address. I know which ones they are. I know why you wish to address the Trial Chamber. But I believe that this can wait until tomorrow, unless there is a housekeeping matter which is so important that you need to address it right now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you've decided that it's going to be tomorrow, then it can remain until tomorrow, but I would like to draw your attention to the following: Because of one of those questions, I'm not in a position to carry out proper cross-examination of this current witness, and you know what this is all about. I wanted to say a few words about that, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead, then. As far as this matter is concerned, yes, you may address this now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So just this one question today, and I leave the other two for tomorrow. Did I understand you right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Judges, on the 29th of September, I received a letter from Hans Holthuis, the Registrar of the Tribunal, two typewritten pages, and I'm being told in this letter that during the course of one month's time, I will not have the possibility of unhindered communication with my legal advisers; that is to say, that they cannot come and pay me unsupervised visits, and I cannot have telephone contacts with them without these contacts being listened in to. The Registrar does refer to some reasons there. He mentions the request of the OTP to impose counsel on him because allegedly I intimidated witnesses through my advisers and carried out this campaign in that way. One of the important reasons that he refers to are information published in the Serbian media, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: (redacted). Now I cannot contact my legal advisers during the cross-examination of this witness. I have no possibility of receiving anything by fax. I heard a few moments ago that if a fax arrives, that it goes to the Registry first, a fax is made -- a photocopy is made, and then I am given only a copy. I will continue to cross-examine witnesses, and I'm going to rely on my own logical reasoning, without recourse to any other material. I assume I am still superior to the OTP in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, at the end of the week the Trial Chamber -- just one moment, Mr. Mundis. I would just like to respond and then you will have the floor. The Trial Chamber received from the Registry a memo last week that specified that it had decided to listen in on your telephone calls between you and your associates, and this was based on the motion filed by the Prosecution, partly based on witness intimidation. The Registrar, in its memo, indicates that you are the one that has orchestrated all of this, on the one hand. And the second point: During your conversations with your associates at the time, you purportedly addressed other issues, issues not related to your Defence case. Therefore, the Registry has decided, pursuant to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, to listen in on your conversations. This procedure is part of our procedure relating to detention matters and provides that you are able to challenge this and refer directly to the President of this Tribunal. The Trial Chamber is not seized of the matter. If you wish to challenge this, you must address yourself to the President of the Tribunal. Contrary to what you have said, the memo of the Registry specifies that you are not prohibited from talking to your associates. You can still talk to your associates and talk to them over the telephone. You can ask them to send you documents for your cross-examination and so on and so forth. So the decision taken by the Registry does not preclude you from speaking with your associates and does not prevent you from turning to them to ask them for information. However, does have, of course, something to do with the client-accused privilege; and if this needs to be addressed, this needs to be addressed by the President of the Tribunal. When your associates send you the documents directly, the Registry then picks up the document and gives it to you straight away. The Registry does not look into the contents of the documents, because this correspondence is confidential. The Registry then pick up the documents that have been faxed to you. Nothing is being secretly photocopied in any way. If anyone were to do this, the person would be committing a serious offence. So, so much for this point. The fact that your telephone is being tapped, well, that might be an issue for you. If that is the case, you must seize the President of the Tribunal. Mr. Mundis, I don't know if you wanted to say anything about this. I assume it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please briefly go into private session, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Two points, very quickly. The Prosecution is not, of course, privy to the letter from the Registrar to the accused, so I'm not familiar with the contents of that letter, other than a press statement that was released. Let me say, however, that as indicated on lines 24 and 25 of page 4, and the first five lines of page 5, it is our understanding that the withdrawal of privileged communications would include documents being transmitted to and from the accused, and to the extent that the accused receives faxes or other documents, it's our understanding that those documents would also be subject to monitoring by the Registry as a form of monitoring communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Mundis, this is not something which I read in the decision handed down by the Registry. What I understood was that the telephone was being tapped. Maybe I stand to be corrected, maybe we need to look into this, but if Mr. Seselj's conversations are being listened in, that's one thing, but if his communications are being monitored, that is another story. But I have noted what you have just told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's my -- it's my understanding, and I stand to be corrected on that point, that all communications are being monitored, and that would include faxes, letters, any form of communication. Otherwise, communication in written form would still be allowed, and that is specifically what is -- what is to be monitored. So I simply wanted to at least put on the record our understanding of what has happened as a result of the Registrar's decision. And the final point, very briefly, just to recall for the benefit of the Trial Chamber with respect to the purported transcripts of conversations between the accused and his associates that he's referred to today, as well as the 23rd of September at our hearing, I do draw the Trial Chamber's attention to page 1414 of the hearings in this case, a status conference on the 20th of August, 2007, in which Mr. Seselj, himself, indicated that his associates were recording the privileged communications that were happening between Mr. Seselj and his associates; and so I would simply like to refresh the Chamber's recollection as to the status conference on the 20th of August, 2007, and particularly page 1414, insofar as that would seem to indicate that his privileged communications were being recorded by his associates for whatever purpose. And at this point, I have nothing further, Your Honours, and Ms. Dahl will be leading the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, we shall call the witness in. The Trial Chamber will scrutinize the Registry's memo. The feeling I have is that the communications had been regulated, but not monitored. We shall address this matter again, and this is something we can address tomorrow. We shall now drop the blinds.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One sentence? I just want to inform you that I have cut off all communications and contacts with my legal advisers. If I am to call them over that telephone that's being listened in to, it can only be private conversations, political and so on. But with regard to the case itself, I have seized all communication. There will be no such communication. Now, you are going to assess the extent to which this is going to affect the fairness of the trial. It never crossed my mind, and I have no reason to complain to the President of the Tribunal. The minimum I had recourse to, as an accused person, has been abolished altogether. Now the only right that I still have is to walk into the courtroom. Perhaps even that's going to be taken away from me. We'll see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Trial Chamber will look at the Registrar's memo again. As far as I understood things, your communications were being regulated, but not prohibited. We shall look into the matter again. Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'd like to have clarified and resolved the question of privileged communication by facsimile with the associates before we begin with this witness. I can discuss that further in private session, but I think that all witness-related security concerns need to be addressed before we allow further privileged communication with respect to cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj has just told us that there's no communication whatsoever between him and his associates, so there's nothing happening for the time being. This is what he's just told us. So we will not address this again. He has just told us that there is no communication.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Respectfully, Your Honour, what he said is that he will not discuss case-related matters on the monitored telephone call. He did not say that he would not be using the facsimile machine that delivers information from his associates into this courtroom, and my understanding of what the Registrar is doing is different from what the Chamber explained before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, are you still using your fax? Is it still working between you and your associates?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... because the telefax is also under control. This is what this decision implies. And I have already been told, when I came into court today, that every fax I receive will first be sent to the Registry, a photocopy will be made there, and only then would the fax be submitted to me. I think that Ms. Dahl is using time up for useless matters, and I could have raised my two issues had she not spent all this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't aware of any of this. I'm extremely surprised about this fact, that the Registrar is photocopying everything you receive. This comes out of the blue, as far as I'm concerned. We shall check this. We have a witness who's about to walk into the courtroom, who has been granted protective measures. Let's drop the blinds, please, Registrar, and let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, I have a very simple question for you, but I'm looking at the clock, and I said we would have a break. After the break, I'll put my question to you. We shall have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Court is back in session. Ms. Dahl, you have the floor. We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: The Presiding Judge had indicated before the break that you wished to pose some questions to the witness. Would you prefer that I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I had a question for you, Witness. You told us that you joined the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party. That's all very well, but what I would like to know is this: All the other volunteers, your comrades, those people that were with you, what was their motive? You explained to us what your motive was. Why were these other people there? Was it because they wanted to defend Serbia? Was it because they wanted to defend Yugoslavia because they were monarchists? Why were they there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Part of the volunteers came from that area, that is to say, from Zvornik or the surrounding area. Others were from Serbia. Some had come because they liked waging war. Zoks, for instance, he liked war. Some people had come either because they liked waging war, because this had become a habit, but then also for the economic benefit, as it were. Some people came on account of patriotism, in addition to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'm interested in is this: Those that were patriots, out of 100, how many were patriots; 50 or so? How many came because they were patriots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if I have to speak in percentage terms, about 20 per cent came for purely patriotic reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So 20 per cent came because they were patriots. Other people came for other reasons. Some because they were interested in war profiteering or 20 per cent as you said were patriots. So I'm sure you were able to talk to these people. What were the reasons for their patriotism?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they talked about the Serbs being under threat as a nation. They said that the Serbs were about to be exterminated by the Muslims and the Croats. Also, they were saying that Serbia was to be defended in Croatia and Bosnia; beforehand in Croatia and now in Bosnia, because if the war were allowed to spill over into Serbia, there would be no Serbia any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. What motivated these patriots, did they ever mention the names of high-profile characters, like Slobodan Milosevic? Did they identify with political figures in any way, or was it a personal form of patriotism which didn't have much to do with political figures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Actually, these are the words of the top people at the time, the people who were in power then. Actually, this is just repetition of their words. At that time, there was this sentence that was repeated time and again that turned into a slogan, "All Serbs in a single state"; that is to say, all Serb territories had to be in a single state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What politician actually said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Milosevic, Mr. Seselj and the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you said "as well as the others." Which others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, other politicians who were in power in Serbia. I don't know all of their names exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question, because I'm going directly to the point now: Those people that talked about Mr. Seselj, were they great in number or did this pertain to a minority of patriots?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there were quite a few of them. He has many supporters and many sympathisers. His word carried a great deal of weight then among the people of Serbia because he portrayed himself as one of the great defenders of the Serb name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you for all your answers. Ms. Dahl, I'll give the floor back to you so that you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Let me follow up on a question by the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was considered a Serb territory that should be in a Serb state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Serb territories in Croatia, the so-called Serb Krajina, and Serb territories in Bosnia-Herzegovina that were called Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we need to be in closed session, and may I ask that the last passage be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall redact line 7, page 25. Page 25 might identify the witness. And then we'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of October, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.20 p.m.,
